name: Path A — Data first
summary: Close the open data questions (odds source, depth charts for all clubs, game-level panel, inactives deadline), then build signals.
pros: Every downstream decision rests on verified, point-in-time official data; validation gates become meaningful.
cons: Slower to produce a visible leaderboard; requires repeated official snapshots.

name: Path B — Strategy first
summary: Prototype the 10 candidate strategies and the leaderboard immediately, with all performance values blank until gates pass.
pros: Fastest visible competition framework and reviewer feedback loop.
cons: Risk of optimising on incomplete data; every strategy stays NOT PASSED until the missing official data arrives.

name: Path C — Review only / hold
summary: Implement nothing beyond documentation and the review gate until a reviewer explicitly chooses a path.
pros: Zero implementation risk; maximum review control.
cons: No progress on own lines, signals or leaderboard operation.
